display.purpose: Hero KPI on analytics; the largest number on a page.

caption.purpose: Meta lines under rows, secondary chart labels. Always muted.

label.purpose: Column heads, badge text, uppercase-tracked metadata.

data.purpose: Numbers in tables, chart tooltips, badge counts. Geist Mono, tabular-nums.

data-display.purpose: The big number on a stat tile. Geist Mono, clamp() sized.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus signal on interactive elements. Never on hover.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, popovers, chart tooltips. Never on static cards.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Standard duration for hover, focus, and background transitions.

motion.name: duration-max
motion.purpose: Ceiling. No interactive transition may exceed this.

motion.name: duration-content-arrival
motion.purpose: Named exception to the 150ms ceiling: highlight fade when a new row arrives unprompted (e.g. live timeline), not a triggered state change.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Sidebar collapses to top bar below this width.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: Second card column enables at this width.

breakpoints.name: ultra
breakpoints.purpose: Stat rows expand from 4 to 6 tiles at this width.

narrative.overview: CC-Track is a control room for a single operator. When the deck lights up, you see three things at once: what is running now, what has been done, and what is still queued. The interface is a status board first, an editor second. Content dominates chrome. On a wide monitor, lanes widen and columns multiply so the deck fills the glass instead of centering a small stage in a sea of margin. The atmosphere is warm graphite: a near-black warm ground (Deep Slate) with the ambient signal of a workshop lit by a single low lamp. Terracotta is the only voice raised on that surface, reserved for what the operator should notice next. Numbers speak in monospace so they align down a column; prose speaks in a modern geometric sans so it stays crisp at large sizes. Nothing is playful, nothing is corporate, nothing is empty. This is a working instrument that a person built for themselves and reaches for daily.
keyCharacteristics: Wide-monitor first: fill the deck, do not center a postage stamp.
Big, decisive type; hierarchy carried by size and weight, not by boxes.
One signal color (terracotta) plus three role colors (sage, ember, indigo). No decorative color.
Flat surfaces at rest; tonal steps for depth; motion only on state.
Data reads in Geist Mono so digits line up without effort.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Terracotta is the only color that raises its voice. It marks what the operator should look at next: the live session, the CTA, the top of a ranking, the primary chart series. If you catch yourself using it decoratively, replace it with Dust or Bone Cream.

rules.name: The Role-Color Discipline Rule
rules.body: Sage means done, Ember means in-flight, Indigo means reference. Never rotate them for palette variety. Rotate through hairline shades of the same role instead.

rules.name: The No-True-Black Rule
rules.body: Deep Slate is warm. Never use #000 on this deck; it flattens the graphite ground and reads as void, not workshop.

rules.name: The Numbers-Are-Mono Rule
rules.body: Any digit that appears next to other digits (stat tile, table cell, chart tooltip, badge count) uses Geist Mono. Prose numbers inside a sentence stay in Geist Sans.

rules.name: The Big Type Rule
rules.body: Display and Data Display use clamp() so the deck grows with the viewport instead of stopping at a laptop-era ceiling. Do not cap the deck at 1200px.

rules.name: The No-Em-Dash Rule
rules.body: Copy uses hyphens, colons, commas, or two sentences. Em dash and en dash are banned in every string the app shows.

rules.name: The Relative Unit Rule
rules.body: Every dimension is expressed in rem, em, ch, vw, %, or clamp(). Pixels are permitted only for hairlines under 2px and for box-shadow blur radii. If you are typing a px value greater than 1, stop and convert to rem.

rules.name: The Fill-The-Deck Rule
rules.body: On monitors wider than 1440px, expand content lanes and add columns. Do not center a narrow deck in a sea of margin. Whitespace has to earn its place by carrying rhythm, not by hiding the operator's data.

rules.name: The Content-First Chrome Rule
rules.body: Chrome (sidebar, headers, dividers) uses Hairline Char at 0.0625rem. It is present, quiet, and never competes with content.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards, tiles, and rows do not carry shadows at rest. If a card looks flat and unimportant, fix the type hierarchy or the border, not the shadow.

rules.name: The Tonal-Depth Rule
rules.body: Where a surface needs to feel on top of another, step one tonal level (Deep to Ink, Ink to Lifted). Never combine tonal step + shadow at rest.

rules.name: The Warm-Corner Rule
rules.body: Every container uses at least 0.375rem radius. Sharp corners belong to another world.

rules.name: The One-Border Rule
rules.body: A tile has exactly one border: 0.0625rem Hairline Char. Nested containers drop the border and rely on tonal step + padding.

dos: Do express every dimension in rem, em, ch, vw, %, or clamp(). Reserve px for 1px hairlines and shadow blur.
Do let the main lane run uncapped from sidebar to viewport edge, and add columns on wide monitors instead of enlarging margins.
Do put every number that shares a column with other numbers in Geist Mono with tabular-nums.
Do use Terracotta Signal for exactly one thing per screen: the current focus target.
Do pair every colored badge with a word or glyph so color-blind operators still parse state.
Do hover to Lifted Slate at 120ms ease-out. Focus-visible gets the Terracotta focus ring.
Do step tonally for depth (Deep to Ink to Lifted) before reaching for a shadow.
donts: Don't use em dashes or en dashes in any string the app shows or any file this project writes. Use a hyphen, colon, or two sentences.
Don't use emoji in UI chrome, empty states, or headers. The geometric glyphs in the sidebar are marks, not emoji, and they stay.
Don't introduce gradients on backgrounds, buttons, or text. Flat, tonal, or hairline only.
Don't use #000 for any ground. The graphite is warm; true black flattens it.

Don't animate anything above 150ms. No bounce, no scale beyond 1.02, no ripple. Preciso y contenido. Exception: content-arrival highlights (e.g. a new live-timeline row) run up to 900ms, since they mark something that just arrived rather than a triggered state change.
Don't center a narrow deck in a wide viewport. Fill the deck.
Don't stack shadows on cards at rest to create depth. Step tonally.
Don't rotate role colors for variety. Sage means done, Ember means in-flight, Indigo means reference, permanently.
Don't cap type at laptop sizes on wide monitors. Display and Data Display use clamp() for a reason.
Don't use zebra striping in tables. Rows are separated by a hairline and by hover state.
